props.gloss_en: R' Yochanan: the day of rain is great, for even armies cease on it
as it is said: 'watering its ridges abundantly, settling its gedudim' (Ps 65:11)
R' Yochanan: rain is withheld only on account of those who pledge charity in public and do not give
as it is said: 'clouds and wind and no rain -- a man who boasts of a false gift' (Prov 25:14)
what is meant by 'you shall surely tithe' (Deut 14:22)? tithe so that you become rich
[the boy:] from where do you know? R' Yochanan: go and test it -- i.e. one may test [God] by tithing
the boy: is it permitted to test the Holy One? but it is written 'you shall not test the Lord' (Deut 6:16)
thus said R' Hoshaya: [testing God is forbidden] except for this one
as it is said: 'bring the whole tithe into the storehouse... and test Me now by this... if I will not open the windows of heaven for you and pour out a blessing ad beli dai' (Mal 3:10)
what is 'ad beli dai'? Rami bar Chama in Rav's name: until your lips wear out from saying 'enough'
the boy: had I reached this verse there, I would not have needed you or Hoshaya your teacher
the boy sitting and reciting: 'the foolishness of man perverts his way, and his heart frets against the Lord' (Prov 19:3)
R' Yochanan, wondering: is there anything written in the Writings that is not alluded to in the Torah? (presupposing: there is not)
the boy: is this then not alluded to? but it is written 'their heart failed them and they turned trembling to one another, saying: what is this that God has done to us?' (Gen 42:28)
R' Yochanan raised his eyes and looked at him; his mother came and took him out, saying: come away from him, lest he do to you as he did to your father
R' Yochanan: rain [comes] for the sake of an individual
sustenance [comes only] for the sake of the many
rain for an individual, as it is written: 'the Lord will open for you His good treasure, to give the rain of your land' (Deut 28:12)
sustenance for the many, as it is written: 'behold I will rain bread for you' (Ex 16:4)
three good providers arose for Israel: Moshe, Aharon and Miriam; and three good gifts were given through them: the well, the cloud and the manna
the well -- in Miriam's merit
the pillar of cloud -- in Aharon's merit
the manna -- in Moshe's merit
Miriam died -- the well departed, as it is said 'and Miriam died there' (Num 20:1), and it is written after it 'and there was no water for the congregation' (Num 20:2)
and [the well] returned in the merit of both [Moshe and Aharon]
Aharon died -- the clouds of glory departed, as it is said 'and the Canaanite, king of Arad, heard' (Num 33:40)
what report did he hear? he heard that Aharon had died and the clouds of glory had departed, and thought he had been given leave to fight Israel
and that is what is written: 'and all the congregation saw that Aharon had died' (Num 20:29)
R' Abbahu: do not read 'and they saw' (vayiru) but 'and they were seen' (vayerau)
Reish Lakish: ki serves in four senses: if, perhaps, but, because
both [the well and the clouds] returned in Moshe's merit
Moshe died -- all of them departed, as it is said 'and I cut off the three shepherds in one month' (Zech 11:8)
but did they die in one month? Miriam died in Nisan, Aharon in Av and Moshe in Adar
rather, it teaches that the three good gifts given through them were annulled, and all departed in one month
Moshe is different: since he asked for the many, he is like the many

Rav Huna bar Manoach, Rav Shmuel bar Idi and Rav Chiyya of Vastanya frequented Rava; when Rava died they came before Rav Pappa, and whenever he told them a teaching that did not seem reasonable to them they would hint to one another; he was distressed
they read to him in his dream: 'and I cut off the three shepherds' (Zech 11:8)
the next day, as they took leave of him, Rav Pappa said to them: let the Rabbis go in peace
